title: Chicago Wabash and Twelfth Street clubs, Benny Harris's gin mill
summary: Sal describes the Chicago nightlife area, black bands like Henry Allen at the gin mill, and his free-spending young days.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: He played with him. I got the picture. And the magazine, man. Oh, yeah? Licking with the women on the floor and all, man. Bix, man. Yeah. Old Bix, man. Yeah. Old Bix, but I got a scene with him. I got a scene with him, man. On Wabash and 12th Street. You know, they called it 12th Street and Roseville Road. They used to the old Greyhound station there. And of course, they had the old Roseville Hotel. And then Michigan Avenue one block over. They had about five blocks. So, from the Fry's Inn and Wabash and Van Buren. By the L, Mr. Turn, going north.
I know she goes pretty good.

Yeah, how about that man? Big, son. And Coliseum was born. Then when they come down here, on with me. You know, if I was saying the wrong or the wrong thing, she wouldn't put it on the tape. Went to here, here. Wipe my hair, you know. I was making money in those days. At that time, see, I had the best seat in the house, man. I was in Monroe right there, man. I wasn't married or nothing, man. Plenty clothes, man. Plenty jeans, you know. That was my life, man. My best sweetheart in the world, my mama. God bless you. Man, we're there. We're on, man. Went to here. I didn't go with them. I had to go to work. But, oh, I went in for nigger joints, man. I remember, I used to go with them in nigger joints, too, you know. In jail, man. Went to Bix and Tronbar, you know. Well, one night, his wife was so, she don't know what's going on, but I went over. I guess I went over there. Oh, man. Then, you know why I never went back there? I thought, Benny Harbour's, you know. You know Benny Harbour's? Yeah, I heard of him. That was the gin mill, see. All that white fellas over there, colored bands, you know. What's that? He used to make the gin in the band, too. Yeah. Fred Marble, Henry Allen, Red Allen, Trumpet, you know. All the greats, you know.
Suede, drumming. All my time was to go back to the drink gin.

Boy, I wonder we were playing the cowards, man. In the color joint, man. And the color joint, man. And the music, man. And the music, man. I was like, you know, I was like, you know, I was like, oh, you know, you know, you know, you know, I was like, oh, I like them now.
And man, he was smarter than me.
He was trying to step away, man. He was throwing me out the glasses. He wouldn't drink it, huh? I'm getting loaded, see.
